metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 5 (Conclusion), selected the title text, changed font from Calibri to Times New Roman via font name field, then saved with Ctrl+S.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select slide, click text boxes, triple-click to select text, type in font name field, change font size, use Enter/Ctrl+S shortcuts.
metadata.explanation: Hardens the original task by combining font change with a size change. The getter downloads 24_8.pptx, checks the last slide title for font_name and font_size_pt. Partial credit: 0.5 for Times New Roman, 0.5 for 54pt (tolerance ±1pt). Original size is 44pt so initial state fails both checks. Title placeholder is identified by shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 (reliable across all PPTX naming conventions). Font name and size fall back to paragraph-level XML (a:defRPr) when run-level attributes are None. [Fixed: replaced truncated 8-char MD5 suffix 'a3587389' with correct 32-char MD5 hash '4b92c85bf54981a99e31cdf8daa555a4' computed from 'edb61b14-a854-4bf5-a075-c8075c11293a|1'] [Fixed: replaced unreliable 'PlaceHolder 1' name-based shape detection with placeholder_format.idx == 0 check; added paragraph-level font fallback for run-level None values]

scoring_breakdown.font_name: 0.5 - Last slide title font is Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.font_size_pt: 0.5 - Last slide title font size is 54pt

fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced invalid 8-char MD5 suffix 'a3587389' with correct 32-char MD5 hash '4b92c85bf54981a99e31cdf8daa555a4' in getter function name, metric function name, evaluator.func, and evaluator.result.type

Fix 2: Replaced unreliable 'PlaceHolder 1' in shape.name check with shape.placeholder_format is not None and shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 to correctly identify title placeholder regardless of naming convention (Title 1 vs PlaceHolder 1)
Fix 3: Added paragraph-level XML fallback (a:defRPr latin/@typeface and a:defRPr/@sz) for when run.font.name or run.font.size is None due to formatting set at paragraph/theme level

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly identifies the last slide using prs.slides[-1] and the title placeholder using shape.placeholder_format.idx == 0 — this is reliable across all PPTX naming conventions (Title 1, PlaceHolder 1, etc.).

Metric correctly handles expected.type='rule': directly accesses expected.get('font_name') and expected.get('font_size_pt') without a nested .get('rules') call, which is the correct pattern when the framework passes the rules dict directly.
Both instruction requirements (font name = Times New Roman, font size = 54pt) are covered with 0.5 partial credit each — coverage is complete.
Font fallback logic walks from run-level to paragraph-level XML (a:defRPr latin/@typeface and a:defRPr/@sz), handling cases where LibreOffice stores formatting above run level.
Expected values (Times New Roman, 54) exactly match the instruction; ±1pt tolerance on size is reasonable for integer rounding.
File-based getter reads saved pptx from disk — no postconfig needed since the task requires saving with Ctrl+S.

Minor residual risk: fallback does not reach slide-layout or theme-level font inheritance. For explicitly user-set fonts (as in this task), run-level or paragraph-level storage is expected, so this is unlikely to cause false negatives.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional robustness: extend the font fallback chain to check slide layout default run properties (slide.slide_layout) if both run-level and paragraph-level return None, to handle rare theme-level font inheritance.
